parts.note_add: Yoke carries the series field coil: S-002 p.5-19 shows the solenoid M terminal feeding the field coil, which feeds the (+) brushes. Test: continuity connector-to-brush, none connector-to-yoke (S-002 p.5-26/5-27, 1985).
The A/T starter is the gear-reduction type (S-002 p.5-3, 5-19, 5-21; this car's catalogue lists a centre bracket and reduction gears). The armature runs in a ball bearing at each end.
4 brushes on the A/T starter (S-038 T:3), two (+) brushes fed from the field coil and two (-) brushes on the grounded plate. Brush wear limit 11.5 mm is SP-071 on PT026.
Front bracket bearing is not sold separately; it is replaced with the bracket (S-002 p.5-25, 5-28). Pinion-gap shims sit between the solenoid and this bracket.
Held by two through-bolts and two brush-holder screws; brush holder and rear bracket are symmetrical and fit either way round (S-002 p.5-23, 5-30).
Held by one installation bolt; behind its cover sit a C washer and an adjusting washer that set the pinion-shaft thrust gap (S-002 p.5-24, 5-29).
Pinion is held by a stop ring in a groove in the pinion shaft; a scarred stop ring must never be reused (S-002 p.5-25, 5-29).
The overrunning clutch is part of the pinion shaft assembly and is replaced as one unit if it slips or binds (S-002 p.5-28).
The armature-shaft gear drives the reduction gear on the pinion shaft; both are greased at assembly (S-002 p.5-29).
The lever is moved by the solenoid plunger and shifts the overrunning clutch and pinion. It must be fitted facing the correct way, and its sliding part is greased (S-002 p.5-19, 5-29).
Ball bearings at both ends of the armature come off with an ordinary bearing puller and go on with a hand press (S-002 p.5-24, 5-28).
